Michael — appreciate the context and the spec PDF. We ran an internal LoadLab focused on your prompt distribution last night; attaching the CSV export (loadlab_results_v1.csv) and a short MAP delta doc (MAP-v3-deltas.pdf). High level summary up front:

- TTFT (time-to-first-token): median ~ 18ms, p95 ~ 65ms for warm KV cache (seq len 180). Cold-start TTFTs spike to ~220ms on first few requests per worker.
- Throughput: single GPU worker sustained ~38k tokens/sec steady-state at concurrency 64. Aggregate pool (8 workers) holds p95 latency targets up to ~480 concurrent sessions in steady-state.
- Burst behavior: when we injected 2x burst (2s ramp to 1.5k concurrent requests), queueing delay grew non-linearly and we observed token reordering on retries in the client harness — indicative of request queue timeout interactions.

Attached is a proposed minimal rate-limit patch (rate_limit_config.patch) that implements a leaky-bucket with a small warmup reserve and a 500ms soft-queue timeout. The plan below is what we can own on Redwood's side if BrightWave confirms:

Action items (Redwood):
- Deliver MAP Addendum (this doc + attached artifacts) — owner: Priya — by EOD today
- Run joint LoadLab with BrightWave traffic replay (test window Wed 04/06 10:00-12:00 PT) — owner: Rishi
- Provide rate-limit config for pilot and a rollback policy (automated fallback to lower-capacity model) — owner: Priyom

Please confirm the joint test window and acceptance criteria (TTFT/p95 throughput) you want in the MAP. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to finalize.

Best,

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP: LoadLab empirical results and rate-limit tuning — technical notes

Michael / team — quick tech notes from the LoadLab run we did against your prompt profile. I'll keep it short and empirical: 

1) KV cache warm-up matters: when concurrency is low and requests are cold, we see TTFT up to ~220ms for the first user tokens per worker. After 8–12 sequences the KV cache amortizes and steady TTFT drops toward the medians Priya quoted. Recommendation: small client-side prefetch (1 warmup request) for first-of-session flows.

2) Burst vs steady-state behavior: steady-state (ramp to 480 concurrent and hold) produced stable p95 latencies ~120–150ms. Bursts (ramp to 1.2k over 2s) created a transient queue that caused p99 spikes >1.4s and increased retry contention on our ingress. The root cause was queue length + request timeout interplay.

3) Rate-limit tuning: tested three profiles — conservative (token-bucket cap 600rps, queue 200ms), balanced (900rps cap, 500ms queue), aggressive (1200rps cap, 800ms queue). Balanced had best throughput without sustained p99 spikes. Aggressive gave better instantaneous throughput but caused downstream tail-latency and retry reorder.

4) Suggested pilot config (for joint Run): implement Balanced profile with a 10% burst reserve and a 500ms soft-queue timeout. Also enable a short client-side backoff jitter to avoid retry storms.

I'll own the joint LoadLab execution and will post a test runbook in the Miro board link.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
